name: Animata
install: npx shadcn@latest add https://animata.design/r/<category>/<slug>.json (per component; site defaults to pnpm: pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add <url>). No npm package - shadcn-style registry + copy-paste. Base deps: npm install tailwindcss tailwind-merge clsx lucide-react (motion optional).
stack: Motion (motion, ex framer-motion) for complex animations
notes: 198 documented components across 23 categories (accordion, background, bento-grid, button, card, carousel, container, fabs, feature-cards, graphs, hero, icon, image, list, overlay, preloader, progress, scroll, section, skeleton, tabs, text, widget), extracted from content/docs/*.mdx in GitHub main (repo ahead of site: 154 published/live in sitemap, 44 have frontmatter published:false and their pages currently 404 until the site deploys them; URLs follow the canonical /docs/<category>/<slug> pattern). Homepage claims "155+ components". Components are copy-paste (no npm package); install per component via shadcn CLI pointing at animata.design/r/<category>/<slug>.json registry. Some components co-locate a .css file. Repo active (last push Aug 2026), 2.7k+ stars, built by codse (Nepal). Every docs page documents usage + manual copy steps.

components.description: The Animated Timeline component is an interactive, visually appealing timeline that responds to user interaction. Built with Framer Motion and React, this component highlights key events or milestones in a vertical timeline structure.When a user hovers over a specific timeline item, the associated circular dot and all previous dots in the sequence turn green, indicating progression. The dot size also enlarges slightly, enhancing the focus on the current event. The component offers a sleek and smooth animation experience, perfect for showcasing chronological steps, milestones, or achievements in an engaging and user-friendly manner.This component is highly customizable, allowing easy modifications to the timeline content and styling, making it suitable for diverse applications such as resumes, project timelines, or product roadmaps.
